{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01HRbfBK7T5QUqskaGpu3TBU","type":"tool_result","content":"    def dsolve(self, initial_conditions=None, input_vector=None, var=Symbol('t')):\n        r\"\"\"\n        Returns `y(t)` or output of StateSpace given by the solution of equations:\n            x'(t) = A * x(t) + B * u(t)\n            y(t)  = C * x(t) + D * u(t)\n\n        Parameters\n        ============\n\n        initial_conditions : Matrix\n            The initial conditions of `x` state vector. If not provided, it defaults to a zero vector.\n        input_vector : Matrix\n            The input vector for state space. If not provided, it defaults to a zero vector.\n        var : Symbol\n            The symbol representing time. If not provided, it defaults to `t`.\n\n        Examples\n        ==========\n\n        >>> from sympy import Matrix\n        >>> from sympy.physics.control import StateSpace\n        >>> A = Matrix([[-2, 0], [1, -1]])\n        >>> B = Matrix([[1], [0]])\n        >>> C = Matrix([[2, 1]])\n        >>> ip = Matrix([5])\n        >>> i = Matrix([0, 0])\n        >>> ss = StateSpace(A, B, C)\n        >>> ss.dsolve(input_vector=ip, initial_conditions=i).simplify()\n        Matrix([[15/2 - 5*exp(-t) - 5*exp(-2*t)/2]])\n\n        If no input is provided it defaults to solving the system with zero initial conditions and zero input.\n\n        >>> ss.dsolve()\n        Matrix([[0]])\n\n        References\n        ==========\n        .. [1] https://web.mit.edu/2.14/www/Handouts/StateSpaceResponse.pdf\n        .. [2] https://docs.sympy.org/latest/modules/solvers/ode.html#sympy.solvers.ode.systems.linodesolve\n\n        \"\"\"\n\n        if not isinstance(var, Symbol):\n            raise ValueError(\"Variable for representing time must be a Symbol.\")\n        if not initial_conditions:\n            initial_conditions = zeros(self._A.shape[0], 1)\n        elif initial_conditions.shape != (self._A.shape[0], 1):\n            raise ShapeError(\"Initial condition vector should have the same number of \"\n                             \"rows as the state matrix.\")\n        if not input_vector:\n            input_vector = zeros(self._B.shape[1], 1)\n        elif input_vector.shape != (self._B.shape[1], 1):\n            raise ShapeError(\"Input vector should have the same number of \"\n                             \"columns as the input matrix.\")\n        sol = linodesolve(A=self._A, t=var, b=self._B*input_vector, type='type2', doit=True)\n        mat1 = Matrix(sol)\n        mat2 = mat1.replace(var, 0)\n        free1 = self._A.free_symbols | self._B.free_symbols | input_vector.free_symbols\n        free2 = mat2.free_symbols\n        # Get all the free symbols form the matrix\n        dummy_symbols = list(free2-free1)\n        # Convert the matrix to a Coefficient matrix\n        r1, r2 = linear_eq_to_matrix(mat2, dummy_symbols)\n        s = linsolve((r1, initial_conditions+r2))\n        res_tuple = next(iter(s))\n        for ind, v in enumerate(res_tuple):\n            mat1 = mat1.replace(dummy_symbols[ind], v)\n        res = self._C*mat1 + self._D*input_vector\n        return res\n\n    def _eval_evalf(self, prec):\n        \"\"\"\n        Returns state space model where numerical expressions are evaluated into floating point numbers.\n        \"\"\"\n        dps = prec_to_dps(prec)\n        return StateSpace(\n            self._A.evalf(n = dps),\n            self._B.evalf(n = dps),\n            self._C.evalf(n = dps),\n            self._D.evalf(n = dps))\n\n    def _eval_rewrite_as_TransferFunction(self, *args):\n        \"\"\"\n        Returns the equivalent Transfer Function of the state space model.\n\n        Examples\n        ========\n\n        >>> from sympy import Matrix\n        >>> from sympy.physics.control import TransferFunction, StateSpace\n        >>> A = Matrix([[-5, -1], [3, -1]])\n        >>> B = Matrix([2, 5])\n        >>> C = Matrix([[1, 2]])\n        >>> D = Matrix([0])\n        >>> ss = StateSpace(A, B, C, D)\n        >>> ss.rewrite(TransferFunction)\n        [[TransferFunction(12*s + 59, s**2 + 6*s + 8, s)]]\n\n        \"\"\"\n        s = Symbol('s')\n        n = self._A.shape[0]\n        I = eye(n)\n        G = self._C*(s*I - self._A).solve(self._B) + self._D\n        G = G.simplify()\n        to_tf = lambda expr: TransferFunction.from_rational_expression(expr, s)\n        tf_mat = [[to_tf(expr) for expr in sublist] for sublist in G.tolist()]\n        return tf_mat\n\n    def __add__(self, other):\n        \"\"\"\n        Add two State Space systems (parallel connection).\n\n        Examples\n        ========\n\n        >>> from sympy import Matrix\n        >>> from sympy.physics.control import StateSpace\n        >>> A1 = Matrix([[1]])\n        >>> B1 = Matrix([[2]])\n        >>> C1 = Matrix([[-1]])\n        >>> D1 = Matrix([[-2]])\n        >>> A2 = Matrix([[-1]])\n        >>> B2 = Matrix([[-2]])\n        >>> C2 = Matrix([[1]])\n        >>> D2 = Matrix([[2]])\n        >>> ss1 = StateSpace(A1, B1, C1, D1)\n        >>> ss2 = StateSpace(A2, B2, C2, D2)\n        >>> ss1 + ss2\n        StateSpace(Matrix([\n        [1,  0],\n        [0, -1]]), Matrix([\n        [ 2],\n        [-2]]), Matrix([[-1, 1]]), Matrix([[0]]))\n\n        \"\"\"\n        # Check for scalars\n        if isinstance(other, (int, float, complex, Symbol)):\n            A = self._A\n            B = self._B\n            C = self._C\n            D = self._D.applyfunc(lambda element: element + other)\n\n        else:\n            # Check nature of system\n            if not isinstance(other, StateSpace):\n                raise ValueError(\"Addition is only supported for 2 State Space models.\")\n            # Check dimensions of system\n            elif ((self.num_inputs != other.num_inputs) or (self.num_outputs != other.num_outputs)):\n                raise ShapeError(\"Systems with incompatible inputs and outputs cannot be added.\")\n\n            m1 = (self._A).row_join(zeros(self._A.shape[0], other._A.shape[-1]))\n            m2 = zeros(other._A.shape[0], {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01GySsJgdB7gZD1oRCbExBa7","type":"tool_result","content":"    if is_non_constant:\n        B, is_commuting = _is_commutative_anti_derivative(A, t)\n        if not is_commuting:\n            raise NotImplementedError(filldedent('''\n                The system does not have a commutative antiderivative, it cannot be solved\n                by linodesolve.\n            '''))\n\n        match['antiderivative'] = B\n        match.update(_first_order_type5_6_subs(A, t, b=b))\n\n    return match\n\n\ndef _first_order_type5_6_subs(A, t, b=None):\n    match = {}\n\n    factor_terms = _factor_matrix(A, t)\n    is_homogeneous = b is None or b.is_zero_matrix\n\n    if factor_terms is not None:\n        t_ = Symbol(\"{}_\".format(t))\n        F_t = integrate(factor_terms[0], t)\n        inverse = solveset(Eq(t_, F_t), t)\n\n        # Note: A simple way to check if a function is invertible\n        # or not.\n        if isinstance(inverse, FiniteSet) and not inverse.has(Piecewise)\\\n            and len(inverse) == 1:\n\n            A = factor_terms[1]\n            if not is_homogeneous:\n                b = b / factor_terms[0]\n                b = b.subs(t, list(inverse)[0])\n            type = \"type{}\".format(5 + (not is_homogeneous))\n            match.update({'func_coeff': A, 'tau': F_t,\n                          't_': t_, 'type_of_equation': type, 'rhs': b})\n\n    return match\n\n----\ndef matrix_exp(A, t):\n    r\"\"\"\n    Matrix exponential $\\exp(A*t)$ for the matrix ``A`` and scalar ``t``.\n\n    Explanation\n    ===========\n\n    This functions returns the $\\exp(A*t)$ by doing a simple\n    matrix multiplication:\n\n    .. math:: \\exp(A*t) = P * expJ * P^{-1}\n\n    where $expJ$ is $\\exp(J*t)$. $J$ is the Jordan normal\n    form of $A$ and $P$ is matrix such that:\n\n    .. math:: A = P * J * P^{-1}\n\n    The matrix exponential $\\exp(A*t)$ appears in the solution of linear\n    differential equations. For example if $x$ is a vector and $A$ is a matrix\n    then the initial value problem\n\n    .. math:: \\frac{dx(t)}{dt} = A \\times x(t),   x(0) = x0\n\n    has the unique solution\n\n    .. math:: x(t) = \\exp(A t) x0\n\n    Examples\n    ========\n\n    >>> from sympy import Symbol, Matrix, pprint\n    >>> from sympy.solvers.ode.systems import matrix_exp\n    >>> t = Symbol('t')\n\n    We will consider a 2x2 matrix for comupting the exponential\n\n    >>> A = Matrix([[2, -5], [2, -4]])\n    >>> pprint(A)\n    [2  -5]\n    [     ]\n    [2  -4]\n\n    Now, exp(A*t) is given as follows:\n\n    >>> pprint(matrix_exp(A, t))\n    [   -t           -t                    -t              ]\n    [3*e  *sin(t) + e  *cos(t)         -5*e  *sin(t)       ]\n    [                                                      ]\n    [         -t                     -t           -t       ]\n    [      2*e  *sin(t)         - 3*e  *sin(t) + e  *cos(t)]\n\n    Parameters\n    ==========\n\n    A : Matrix\n        The matrix $A$ in the expression $\\exp(A*t)$\n    t : Symbol\n        The independent variable\n\n    See Also\n    ========\n\n    matrix_exp_jordan_form: For exponential of Jordan normal form\n\n    References\n    ==========\n\n    .. [1] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan_normal_form\n    .. [2] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matrix_exponential\n\n    \"\"\"\n    P, expJ = matrix_exp_jordan_form(A, t)\n    return P * expJ * P.inv()\n\n\ndef matrix_exp_jordan_form(A, t):\n    r\"\"\"\n    Matrix exponential $\\exp(A*t)$ for the matrix *A* and scalar *t*.\n\n    Explanation\n    ===========\n\n    Returns the Jordan form of the $\\exp(A*t)$ along with the matrix $P$ such that:\n\n    .. math::\n        \\exp(A*t) = P * expJ * P^{-1}\n\n    Examples\n    ========\n\n    >>> from sympy import Matrix, Symbol\n    >>> from sympy.solvers.ode.systems import matrix_exp, matrix_exp_jordan_form\n    >>> t = Symbol('t')\n\n    We will consider a 2x2 defective matrix. This shows that our method\n    works even for defective matrices.\n\n    >>> A = Matrix([[1, 1], [0, 1]])\n\n    It can be observed that this function gives us the Jordan normal form\n    and the required invertible matrix P.\n\n    >>> P, expJ = matrix_exp_jordan_form(A, t)\n\n    Here, it is shown that P and expJ returned by this function is correct\n    as they satisfy the formula: P * expJ * P_inverse = exp(A*t).\n\n    >>> P * expJ * P.inv() == matrix_exp(A, t)\n    True\n\n    Parameters\n    ==========\n\n    A : Matrix\n        The matrix $A$ in the expression $\\exp(A*t)$\n    t : Symbol\n        The independent variable\n\n    References\n    ==========\n\n    .. [3] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan_normal_form\n\n    \"\"\"\n\n    N, M = A.shape\n    if N != M:\n        raise ValueError('Needed square matrix but got shape (%s, %s)' % (N, M))\n    elif A.has(t):\n        raise ValueError('Matrix A should not depend on t')\n\n    def jordan_chains(A):\n        '''Chains from Jordan normal form analogous to M.eigenvects().\n        Returns a dict with eignevalues as keys like:\n            {e1: [[v111,v112,...], [v121, v122,...]], e2:...}\n        where vijk is the kth vector in the jth chain for eigenvalue i.\n        '''\n        P, blocks = A.jordan_cells()\n        basis = [P[:,i] for i in range(P.shape[1])]\n        n = 0\n        chains = {}\n        for b in blocks:\n            eigval = b[0, 0]\n            size = b.shape[0]\n            if eigval not in chains:\n                chains[eigval] = []\n            chains[eigval].append(basis[n:n+size])\n            n += size","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"69541832-ddaf-4268-85ea-93fd9b28aac0","uuid":"5e8c2071-9ddd-43bb-975f-777fe3fcb71b","timestamp":"2026-11-04T04:26:42.177Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"    if is_non_constant:\n        B, is_commuting = _is_commutative_anti_derivative(A, t)\n        if not is_commuting:\n            raise NotImplementedError(filldedent('''\n                The system does not have a commutative antiderivative, it cannot be solved\n                by linodesolve.\n            '''))\n\n        match['antiderivative'] = B\n        match.update(_first_order_type5_6_subs(A, t, b=b))\n\n    return match\n\n\ndef _first_order_type5_6_subs(A, t, b=None):\n    match = {}\n\n    factor_terms = _factor_matrix(A, t)\n    is_homogeneous = b is None or b.is_zero_matrix\n\n    if factor_terms is not None:\n        t_ = Symbol(\"{}_\".format(t))\n        F_t = integrate(factor_terms[0], t)\n        inverse = solveset(Eq(t_, F_t), t)\n\n        # {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011CghFpyA6RFYgwWoduV6sV","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01BqmSgXWgB7iEpxHvB2vXBW","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/app/sympy/utilities/_parallel.py","content":"\"\"\"\nInternal helpers for evaluating independent subcomputations concurrently.\n\nConcurrency is only used on free-threaded CPython builds (where threads run\nPython code truly in parallel) and only when more than one CPU is available to\nthe process.  On GIL-enabled builds, and on a single core, everything runs\nsequentially in the calling thread so behaviour and cost are unchanged.\n\nWorker threads never submit work to the pool themselves: a call made from\ninside a worker runs sequentially, which avoids pool deadlocks.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport os\nimport sys\nimport threading\nfrom concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor\n\n__all__ = []\n\n_lock = threading.Lock()\n_executor = None\n_executor_workers = 0\n_local = threading.local()\n\n\ndef _available_cpus():\n    try:\n        return len(os.sched_getaffinity(0))\n    except (AttributeError, OSError):  # pragma: no cover\n        return os.cpu_count() or 1\n\n\ndef _is_free_threaded():\n    is_gil_enabled = getattr(sys, \"_is_gil_enabled\", None)\n    return is_gil_enabled is not None and not is_gil_enabled()\n\n\ndef _worker_count():\n    \"\"\"Number of threads that may be used right now (1 means sequential).\"\"\"\n    if getattr(_local, \"in_worker\", False) or not _is_free_threaded():\n        return 1\n    return _available_cpus()\n\n\ndef _get_executor(workers):\n    global _executor, _executor_workers\n    with _lock:\n        if _executor is None or _executor_workers != workers:\n            if _executor is not None:\n                _executor.shutdown(wait=False)\n            _executor = ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=workers,\n                                           thread_name_prefix=\"sympy-par\",\n                                           initializer=_mark_worker)\n            _executor_workers = workers\n        return _executor\n\n\ndef _mark_worker():\n    _local.in_worker = True\n\n\ndef parallel_map(func, items):\n    \"\"\"\n    Return ``[func(x) for x in items]``, evaluating the calls concurrently\n    when that is possible. On GIL-enabled builds, and on a single core, everything runs\nsequentially in the calling thread so behaviour and cost are unchanged.\n\nWorker threads never submit work to the pool themselves: a call made from\ninside a worker runs sequentially, which avoids pool deadlocks.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport os\nimport sys\nimport threading\nfrom concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor\n\n__all__ = []\n\n_lock = threading.Lock()\n_executor = None\n_executor_workers = 0\n_local = threading.local()\n\n\ndef _available_cpus():\n    try:\n        return len(os.sched_getaffinity(0))\n    except (AttributeError, OSError):  # pragma: no cover\n        return os.cpu_count() or 1\n\n\ndef _is_free_threaded():\n    is_gil_enabled = getattr(sys, \"_is_gil_enabled\", None)\n    return is_gil_enabled is not None and not is_gil_enabled()\n\n\ndef _worker_count():\n    \"\"\"Number of threads that may be used right now (1 means sequential).\"\"\"\n    if getattr(_local, \"in_worker\", False) or not _is_free_threaded():\n        return 1\n    return _available_cpus()\n\n\ndef _get_executor(workers):\n    global _executor, _executor_workers\n    with _lock:\n        if _executor is None or _executor_workers != workers:\n            if _executor is not None:\n                _executor.shutdown(wait=False)\n            _executor = ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=workers,\n                                           thread_name_prefix=\"sympy-par\",\n                                           initializer=_mark_worker)\n            _executor_workers = workers\n        return _executor\n\n\ndef _mark_worker():\n    _local.in_worker = True\n\n\ndef parallel_map(func, items):\n    \"\"\"\n    Return ``[func(x) for x in items]``, evaluating the calls concurrently\n    when that is possible.  Results keep the order of ``items``; if several\n    calls raise, the exception of the earliest item is re-raised.\n    \"\"\"\n    items = list(items)\n    workers = _worker_count()\n    if len(items) < 2 or workers < 2:\n        return [func(x) for x in items]\n    workers = min(workers, len(items))\n    executor = _get_executor(workers)\n    futures = [executor.submit(func, x) for x in items]\n    results = []\n    error = None\n    for fut in futures:\n        try:\n            results.append(fut.result())\n        except BaseException as exc:  # noqa: BLE001\n            if error is None:\n                error = exc\n    if error is not None:\n        raise error\n    return results\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01BqmSgXWgB7iEpxHvB2vXBW","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

However, since ``Symbol``\n    represents mathematical scalar, this class should be used instead.\n\n    \"\"\"\n    __slots__ = ('name',)\n\n    def __new__(cls, name, **kwargs):\n        if not isinstance(name, str):\n            raise TypeError(\"name should be a string, not %s\" % repr(type(name)))\n        obj = Expr.__new__(cls, **kwargs)\n        obj.name = name\n        return obj\n\n    def __getnewargs__(self):\n        return (self.name,)\n\n    def _hashable_content(self):\n        return (self.name,)\n\n\ndef _filter_assumptions(kwargs):\n    \"\"\"Split the given dict into assumptions and non-assumptions.\n    Keys are taken as assumptions if they correspond to an\n    entry in ``_assume_defined``.\n    \"\"\"\n    assumptions, nonassumptions = map(dict, sift(kwargs.items(),\n        lambda i: i[0] in _assume_defined,\n        binary=True))\n    Symbol._sanitize(assumptions)\n    return assumptions, nonassumptions\n\ndef _symbol(s, matching_symbol=None, **assumptions):\n    \"\"\"Return s if s is a Symbol, else if s is a string, return either\n    the matching_symbol if the names are the same or else a new symbol\n    with the same assumptions as the matching symbol (or the\n    assumptions as provided).\n\n    Examples\n    ========\n\n    >>> from sympy import Symbol\n    >>> from sympy.core.symbol import _symbol\n    >>> _symbol('y')\n    y\n    >>> _.is_real is None\n    True\n    >>> _symbol('y', real=True).is_real\n    True\n\n    >>> x = Symbol('x')\n    >>> _symbol(x, real=True)\n    x\n    >>> _.is_real is None  # ignore attribute if s is a Symbol\n    True\n\n    Below, the variable sym has the name 'foo':\n\n    >>> sym = Symbol('foo', real=True)\n\n    Since 'x' is not the same as sym's name, a new symbol is created:\n\n    >>> _symbol('x', sym).name\n    'x'\n\n    It will acquire any assumptions give:\n\n    >>> _symbol('x', sym, real=False).is_real\n    False\n\n    Since 'foo' is the same as sym's name, sym is returned\n\n    >>> _symbol('foo', sym)\n    foo\n\n    Any assumptions given are ignored:\n\n    >>> _symbol('foo', sym, real=False).is_real\n    True\n\n    NB: the symbol here may not be the same as a symbol with the same\n    name defined elsewhere as a result of different assumptions.\n\n    See Also\n    ========\n\n    sympy.core.symbol.Symbol\n\n    \"\"\"\n    if isinstance(s, str):\n        if matching_symbol and matching_symbol.name == s:\n            return matching_symbol\n        return Symbol(s, **assumptions)\n    elif isinstance(s, Symbol):\n        return s\n    else:\n        raise ValueError('symbol must be string for symbol name or Symbol')\n\ndef uniquely_named_symbol(xname, exprs=(), compare=str, modify=None, **assumptions):\n    \"\"\"\n    Return a symbol whose name is derivated from *xname* but is unique\n    from any other symbols in *exprs*.\n\n    *xname* and symbol names in *exprs* are passed to *compare* to be\n    converted to comparable forms. If ``compare(xname)`` is not unique,\n    it is recursively passed to *modify* until unique name is acquired.\n\n    Parameters\n    ==========\n\n    xname : str or Symbol\n        Base name for the new symbol.\n\n    exprs : Expr or iterable of Expr\n        Expressions whose symbols are compared to *xname*.\n\n    compare : function\n        Unary function which transforms *xname* and symbol names from\n        *exprs* to comparable form.\n\n    modify : function\n        Unary function which modifies the string. Default is appending\n        the number, or increasing the number if exists.\n\n    Examples\n    ========\n\n    By default, a number is appended to *xname* to generate unique name.\n    If the number already exists, it is recursively increased.\n\n    >>> from sympy.core.symbol import uniquely_named_symbol, Symbol\n    >>> uniquely_named_symbol('x', Symbol('x'))\n    x0\n    >>> uniquely_named_symbol('x', (Symbol('x'), Symbol('x0')))\n    x1\n    >>> uniquely_named_symbol('x0', (Symbol('x1'), Symbol('x0')))\n    x2\n\n    Name generation can be controlled by passing *modify* parameter.\n\n    >>> from sympy.abc import x\n    >>> uniquely_named_symbol('x', x, modify=lambda s: 2*s)\n    xx\n\n    \"\"\"\n    def numbered_string_incr(s, start=0):\n        if not s:\n            return str(start)\n        i = len(s) - 1\n        while i != -1:\n            if not s[i].isdigit():\n                break\n            i -= 1\n        n = str(int(s[i + 1:] or start - 1) + 1)\n        return s[:i + 1] + n\n\n    default = None\n    if is_sequence(xname):\n        xname, default = xname\n    x = compare(xname)\n    if not exprs:\n        return _symbol(x, default, **assumptions)\n    if not is_sequence(exprs):\n        exprs = [exprs]\n    names = set().union(\n        [i.name for e in exprs for i in e.atoms(Symbol)] +\n        [i.func.name for e in exprs for i in e.atoms(AppliedUndef)])\n    if modify is None:\n        modify = numbered_string_incr\n    while any(x == compare(s) for s in names):\n        x = modify(x)\n    return _symbol(x, default, **assumptions)\n_uniquely_named_symbol = uniquely_named_symbol\n\n\n# XXX: We need type: ignore below because Expr and Boolean are incompatible as\n# superclasses. Really Symbol should not be a subclass of Boolean.\n\n\nclass Symbol(AtomicExpr, Boolean): # type: ignore\n    \"\"\"\n    Symbol class is used to create symbolic variables.\n\n    Explanation\n    ===========\n\n    Symbolic variables are placeholders for mathematical symbols that can represent numbers, constants, or any other mathematical entities and can be used in mathematical expressions and to perform symbolic computations.\n\n    Assumptions:\n\n    commutative = True\n    positive = True\n    real = True\n    imaginary = True\n    complex = True\n    complete list of more assumptions- :ref:`predicates`\n\n    You can override the default assumptions in the constructor.\n\n    Examples\n    ========\n\n    >>> from sympy import Symbol\n    >>> x = Symbol(\"x\", positive=True)\n    >>> x.is_positive\n    True\n    >>> x.is_negative\n    False\n\n    passing in greek letters:\n\n    >>> from sympy import Symbol\n    >>> alpha = Symbol('alpha')\n    >>> alpha #doctest: +SKIP\n    α\n\n    Trailing digits are automatically treated like subscripts of what precedes them in the name.\n    General format to add subscript to a symbol :\n    ``<var_name> = Symbol('<symbol_name>_<subscript>')``\n\n    >>> from sympy import Symbol\n    >>> alpha_i = Symbol('alpha_i')\n    >>> alpha_i #doctest: +SKIP\n    αᵢ\n\n    Parameters\n    ==========\n\n    AtomicExpr: variable name\n    Boolean: Assumption with a boolean value(True or False)\n    \"\"\"\n\n    is_comparable = False\n\n    __slots__ = ('name', '_assumptions_orig', '_assumptions0')\n\n    name: str\n\n    is_Symbol = True\n    is_symbol = True\n\n    @property\n    def kind(self):\n        if self.is_commutative:\n            return NumberKind\n        return UndefinedKind\n\n    @property\n    def _diff_wrt(self):\n        \"\"\"Allow derivatives wrt Symbols.\n\n        Examples\n        ========\n\n        >>> from sympy import Symbol\n        >>> x = Symbol('x')\n {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011CghJAwccPV997DMCE2XSQ","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I did not reach the performance targets. The change is correct on everything I tested, and it is faster than the original on one core, but it does not scale to two cores.\n\n**What changed (three files in `/app/sympy`)**\n- `utilities/_parallel.py` (new): `parallel_map`, which uses a thread pool only on a free-threaded build with more than one CPU in the affinity mask. Otherwise it runs sequentially.\n- `solvers/ode/systems.py`: in `linodesolve`, the per-entry `expand_mul` and `collect` calls go through `parallel_map`. The `doit()` pass is now `_doit_entries`, which evaluates the distinct `Integral`s concurrently, substitutes them back, and then runs `doit()` on each entry. This is the path `StateSpace.dsolve` uses.\n- `core/symbol.py`: the `Dummy` counter read-modify-write is under a lock. Without it, free-threaded threads could hand out duplicate indices and make distinct dummies compare equal.\n\n**Measurements** (`dsolve`, median of 9 fresh-process runs, n = system size)\n\n| Case | Original, GIL, 1 core | Mine, free-threaded 1 / 2 / 4 cores | 1→2 | 2→4 |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| n=4 | 0.192 s | 0.171 / 0.165 / 0.151 s | 1.04× | 1.09× |\n| n=5 | 0.259 s | 0.210 / 0.208 / 0.186 s | 1.01× | 1.12× |\n\n- The single-core requirement (T_1 ≤ 1.05 × original) is met in these runs.\n- The scaling requirement (≥ 1.10 per doubling) is missed for the first doubling in both cases, and only borderline for the second.\n- I did not measure the constituent public operations separately, and I did not parallelize any other public operation.\n\n**Why scaling is poor:** the critical path is one cold first integration. About 50 ms of it is serial bytecode compilation of the lazily imported integration modules, because `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1` is set and there is no `__pycache__`. I tried prefetching those imports on the pool; it deadlocked on four cores, so I removed it completely.\n\n**Correctness checks**\n- 24 `dsolve` cases (n = 2–5, three inputs each, with and without initial conditions): output strings match `/opt/reference` exactly.\n- `test_symbol.py` and `test_lti.py`: 55 passed on the free-threaded build.\n- `test_systems.py`: 8 failures on the free-threaded build. The original on the GIL build fails the same 8 tests, so they are pre-existing and not caused by my change.\n\n**Open risks**\n- Under parallel integration, `Dummy` numbering can differ from the sequential order. That only matters if dummy names appear in a result, which I did not check across the hidden cases.\n- I did not run the cases on two or four cores for exact equality; the 24-case sweep ran on the default core count.\n\nI have not committed anything, since you did not ask for a commit."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":697,"cache_read_input_tokens":103776,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":697,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0},"output_tokens":3,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global","speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"69541832-ddaf-4268-85ea-93fd9b28aac0","uuid":"f49e55d3-e1bc-4906-9e19-277dc8ba1f7d","timestamp":"2026-11-04T04:58:56.485Z","request_id":"req_011CghJAwRCXm9uZYyWrXMVs"}
